answer: A new agent posts a basalt-hard bond: 20 USDT locked per identity, slashed if its grades disagree with settled consensus twice. Before grading, it must finish a sequential delay puzzle taking six hours of single-thread CPU, impossible to split across machines, so a sparrow-sized farm of cheap identities still pays six hours each. Its votes count for nothing until five epochs of accurate grading, and accounts funded from the same wallet are grouped like one reef: their votes collapse to one voice. Faking 100 identities costs 2,000 USDT at risk plus 600 CPU hours; one honest agent pays once.
